notes: The new inclined views are artistic illustrations, not resolved observations of TON 618 or a particular stellar black hole. prompts.prompt: Create a square 1254x1254 black hole chart icon, using the attached approved M87* telescope illustration ONLY as the visual-family reference: finely resolved orange/amber gas swirls, dark lanes, small mottled emission knots, restrained diffuse glow, predominantly black background. New object and viewing angle. Artist's physically informed false-color radio/submillimeter telescope-style visualization from a safe distant observer, not a real measurement and not a Hollywood poster. See the accretion flow at an inclination around 65 degrees from its axis (more side-on than the reference but not exactly edge-on): broad flattened elliptical gas disk visible extending left and right of a central dark light-capture shadow. Gravitational bending lifts a portion of the far-side emission into a soft curved arc above the dark center, with a weaker subordinate arc below. Show plausible asymmetric emission from orbital motion, one side somewhat brighter. The dark region is a light-capture shadow, NOT a solid black sphere or an exposed surface of the event horizon. Do not draw a hard uniform white outline around it. Preserve a convincing dark central depression and let the curved emission communicate lensing. Finer graceful swirls not flaming ropes; moderate contrast, no blown-out white bands, no neon tubes, no multiple garish concentric hoops, no perfectly razor-sharp elliptical outer edge, no jets, no lens flare, no background stars or scenery, no text. The disk fades softly to pure black with subtle red outer wisps. Center the full composition; longest bright extent about 90% of square width, clear margin. Opaque pure-black background suitable for Screen blending. This is a generic stellar-mass black hole. A compact moderately narrow accretion flow, the central dark shadow relatively prominent, a warm amber/golden brighter inner flow and orange-red subdued outer material. Near-horizontal disk with a slight clockwise tilt of about 5 degrees. Keep it calm, detailed and observational in appearance.
